engagement_title: Norvant March release launch kit: cut a forty one minute founder take into an explainer and a vertical that keeps her and the product in frame, pull six press frames to one look, recover the wordmark off the reception sign, and rebuild the printer's card into a live eleven city run
vertical: Technology, B2B SaaS, an eleven person workflow automation product sold to finance and operations teams (Minneapolis, Minnesota)
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the Freelancer.com motion graphics brief carried in the ledger, in which a client with raw explainer footage, a logo, colour references and a loose outline wants a clear informative cut plus on brand text treatment (lower thirds, call outs, title and end cards) and the linked assets organised so the team can make future tweaks themselves. Co anchored to the same client's stated need for a launch package rather than a single video. REPOSITIONED for connector reality, which is what makes this the honest fuller commission. The headless connector cannot composite type onto a video track, so the on brand text half of the real brief is delivered where it can genuinely be made and edited: press frames pulled from the cut and graded, an announcement canvas set authored as a native editable document, and the eleven city printed cards built as a live merge off the printer's own file. The tightening is done by the shortening route, which chooses its own retained set, and the vertical is a ratio reframe rather than a re shoot. The company is laundered to the coined fictional Norvant, a workflow automation product whose identity is a hexring glyph and a slate and amber wordmark; no real company, product, person or trademark is named, and Freelancer.com is only the sourcing platform.
client_one_liner: Our founder talked for forty one minutes in one take with the product on the monitor beside her, we have eleven city events in March, and last year's card exists only as the file that went to the printer.
client_brief:
Norvant, launch kit for the March release

Norvant is workflow automation for finance and operations teams. Seats are one hundred and forty dollars a month and nothing gets bought without three people signing off, so everything we put out has to look like it was made by people who know what they are doing. We are eleven people and we have no designer.

In March we ship the release the whole company has been building toward, and we run eleven evening events, one per city, for customers and prospects.

What we have. Our founder sat down and talked for forty one minutes in one take about why the product exists and how it works, with the product up on the monitor beside her. It is good material and it is far too long. The room had a hum and she is quiet.

What we need. A short explainer for the top of the site, cut from that take, with the audio fixed so someone in procurement watching on laptop speakers hears every word. The same explainer as a vertical for the feeds, same length. Six still frames pulled out of it for the press kit and the blog, all looking like the same day.

For the eleven events we need printed cards, one per city, carrying that city's venue, date, host and seat line. Last year's card is attached exactly as it went to our printer. We want this year's run built from that so the cards match, and we want the file back so we can run it again in the autumn.

We also need an announcement set for the site and the feeds that we can edit ourselves, because the date will move at least once.

Our mark only survives as the sign on our reception wall. The original file went with the agency.

Slate and amber, quiet, no stock smiles. Tell us plainly what you could not do and why. We would rather know now.
price_band_and_audience: A one hundred and forty dollar per seat per month B2B product bought by a committee of three in finance and operations, with a procurement review in the middle of the cycle. The band is load bearing. At this price the buyer is looking for evidence of seriousness, so the kit has to be quiet, specific and legible: a founder who sounds like she knows the domain, press frames that show the actual product, a printed card that looks like it came from a company with a controller, and type that is plain rather than expressive. The same product at a nine dollar self serve band would correctly be launched loud, bright, animated and benefit led, and shipping that here reads as consumer marketing and lengthens the sales cycle because the committee stops believing the numbers. Push the other way into enterprise grey, stock boardrooms and a dense capability matrix and it misprices a product an operations lead adopts in an afternoon. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 1,800 to 3,800 dollars fixed.

brand_identity.tagline: Workflow automation for finance and operations.
brand_identity.founded_place_size: Founded 2022 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. An eleven person company with no in-house designer.
brand_identity.about: Norvant is workflow automation built for finance and operations teams. Seats are one hundred and forty dollars a month, and nothing gets bought without three people signing off, so everything we put out has to look like it was made by people who know what they are doing. We are a small team shipping a serious tool, and our March release is the work the whole company has been building toward.
brand_identity.audience: A buying committee of three in finance and operations, with a procurement review mid-cycle. They are looking for evidence of seriousness and real numbers, and they lengthen the cycle the moment something feels like consumer marketing.
brand_identity.price_positioning: Considered B2B mid-market. One hundred and forty dollars per seat per month, committee-approved. Not self-serve impulse software, and not heavyweight enterprise. A tool an operations lead can adopt in an afternoon and defend to a controller.
brand_identity.typography: One quiet, credible type system across the cards, the announcement set and the handover: a plain neutral face for detail and body, a measured companion for headings. Nothing expressive, nothing decorative. Legibility at small print sizes matters more than personality.
brand_identity.voice: Plain, specific, confident without selling. States what the product does and lets the facts carry it. No stock smiles, no superlatives. Tells people directly what is and is not true.
brand_identity.brand_assets_status: Brand files went with the agency that made them. The mark now survives only as the sign on our reception wall: a hexring glyph beside the wordmark, cut in slate on a brushed metal panel. Last year's regional event card exists only as the print-ready file we sent to the printer. We need the mark recovered as scalable artwork and this year's card run rebuilt from last year's file so it matches. No editable logo source, colour build or master template remains on our side.
brand_identity.values: Seriousness you can verify, restraint over noise, and plain honesty about what we could and could not do.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_founder_take.mp4
assets_supplied.kind: A single take founder interview, forty one minutes, 1920x1080, shot on a tripod in the company's meeting room: the founder seated frame left, the product running on a monitor frame right, a window wall behind.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Elise talking for forty one minutes about why we built it. The room had a hum and she is quiet."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The framing puts the two things that matter at opposite edges with a stretch of empty table between them, so any centre anchored reframe to a vertical ratio keeps the emptiness and takes the side of her face and the monitor with it, while returning a clean, sharp, plausible vertical at full success. She also stands up and re seats at roughly minute thirty two and comes back sitting further left, so no single anchor serves the whole take, and the monitor picks up the window wall as a bright reflection for the first eleven minutes only.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_launch_card_2025.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: Last year's regional event card exactly as it was sent to the printer: a 105 by 148 millimetre card with the event details set as one continuous block and a placed portrait of that city's host.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Last year's card, straight from our printer. We want this year to match it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Its details are set as a continuous flow, so the converted layout does not expose one frame per field, and the readout that reports the frame's text back to you omits one run entirely while keeping the line break that followed it, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past that point is short by the length of the dropped run. The validator returns valid on those wrong offsets and the placeholder step reports success, and the missing fields appear nowhere until a card is actually merged and looked at. The file also carries no bleed at all, which cannot be introduced afterward.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_events.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The eleven city event roster: city, venue, street address, date, host name, host title, seat tier line, and a column of per city venue photographs.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The eleven cities. One row each, with the venue picture for that city."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two venue names run long enough that at the card's fixed detail measure the line does not spill or reflow, it simply stops rendering and truncates at the trim edge, which looks like a design choice on a proof. One city appears twice with two different venues because the roster was merged from two spreadsheets, one date is written in a different order from the other ten, and one row's seat tier line is the field the readout drops.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_reception_sign.jpg
assets_supplied.kind: A handheld photograph of the reception wall sign: a hexring glyph beside the wordmark, cut in slate on a brushed metal panel under a raking downlight.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The sign on our wall. It is the only place the mark still exists at any size."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The glyph is an enclosed ring with a fine internal counter, so background removal returns a solid opaque disc rather than a ring, and a trace that looks clean at full canvas closes that counter at the size the mark actually reproduces on a 105 millimetre card and on an amber ground. The slate cut also runs close to the brushed panel in value across the left third where the downlight falls off, so a selection there takes panel with the ink.

assets_supplied.name: norvant_launch_copy.txt
assets_supplied.kind: The approved launch copy: the release name, the three claims legal cleared, the six press frame captions and the standing event card wording.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The copy as cleared. The three claims cannot be reworded."

acceptance_bar: The explainer still explains. What the product does and why it exists both survive into the delivered cut, and the cut does not end on a sentence the founder did not finish.
The delivered audio master is intelligible on laptop speakers at office volume, and the founder still sounds like a person in a meeting room rather than a synthesised voice.

In the vertical, the founder and the product are both in frame for the whole running length, including after she re seats. A vertical that is technically the right ratio but has lost one of them fails.
The vertical is the same length as the explainer and neither exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source take. Nothing is enlarged to reach a frame.
The six press frames read as one day: one white point, one black point, one treatment of the window wall behind her, and six genuinely different moments rather than one frame cut six ways.
Eleven cards are produced, one per city, one record per page, in roster order, and every field on every card renders in full. A card that ends a venue name at the trim edge is not a card.
The per city venue picture on each card is that city's picture. One picture standing in for eleven fails even though it renders.
The merge template comes back as a live reusable file that still carries every field, so the autumn run can be made without repeating this work.

The mark is placeable artwork rather than a picture of artwork: transparent, scalable with a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding underneath, and the ring still reads as a ring at the size it reproduces on the card and on the amber ground.

The announcement set arrives as one working file the team can retype, with live text in one type system, the mark as live vector, and every frame carried as embedded image data rather than a reference.
One type system across the cards, the announcement set and the handover, with the note naming per role the family, its foundry or designer, and the actual weight used.
The note states plainly what could not be done and why, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation, and the limits of the merge file being handed back.

adobe_surfaces.tools: video_metadata, video_render_frame, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut, video_resize
adobe_surfaces.role: The founder take from end to end. It reads what the take actually is and where in the frame the two subjects sit, cleans a quiet voice recorded in a room with a hum, shortens forty one minutes toward an explainer a procurement reviewer will finish, produces the same length vertical by ratio reframe without enlargement, and yields the six press frames out of the finished cut. Each of these routes returns a plausible result whatever it did, so the surface is only usable if every output is inspected by rendering frames from it and summarising it.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Photoshop and Lightroom imaging, including image_vectorize which is counted HERE and not as an Illustrator surface
adobe_surfaces.tools: asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload, asset_inline_preview, image_apply_adjustments (masked and unmasked), image_apply_auto_tone, image_select_by_prompt (returnBbox), image_invert_selection, image_crop_to_bounds, image_crop_and_resize (reading metadata.tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor), image_fill_area, image_remove_background, image_vectorize
adobe_surfaces.role: Every still decision. It brings six frames pulled from one take to one press look with confined corrections where the window wall behind her blows out and where the monitor carries a reflection for the first eleven minutes, cuts each frame to the ratio its destination needs while reading the returned tradeoffs rather than the success message, prepares the eleven venue pictures to one treatment for the merge, and recovers the wordmark and the hexring at ink level off a photographed sign with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

adobe_surfaces.tools: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt (including its validator mode), prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout, document_render_layout
adobe_surfaces.role: The eleven city card run, built off the printer's own file so this year matches last year. This is the only surface that does one record per page at volume, and the entire job rests on what the conversion actually exposes: the real frame inventory has to be read out of the exported document structure, the true story text has to be reconstructed from the document's own content runs before a single offset is computed, and every placeholder has to be re verified after the template is prepared, because both the validator and the placeholder step report success on a template that is silently missing fields.

adobe_surfaces.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring to a native editable document
adobe_surfaces.tools: get_account_type, create_visual_design_express_skill, html_export_readiness_skill, asset_initialize_file_upload / asset_finalize_file_upload with media_type text/html, export_html_to_express({url}), asset_search (CCAsset), asset_get_presigned_urls, asset_inline_preview
adobe_surfaces.role: The announcement set as one native editable document carrying a wide, a square and a tall canvas, which is the only surface in the connector that composes free form fixed canvas layout and the only route to the working file the team asked for because the date will move. Every press frame must be pulled down and inlined as image data because a URL renders as an empty grey box at full success, the mark goes in as inline SVG so it stays vector, and family and weight are declared on every text element.

adobe_surfaces.tools: font_recommend (once per typographic role), font_styles, find_fonts, get_fontkit_embed_url
adobe_surfaces.role: The type system for the announcement set and the handover, and the reference the printed card is judged against. The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on quiet and credible for a committee rather than expressive. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently. The note has to be honest that this typography reaches the announcement set and not the merged card, which carries the printer's own faces.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching anything.
trajectory.judgement: The cut, the vertical and the audio are video work; eleven personalised cards are a record per page merge and belong nowhere else; the announcement set has to be an authored fixed canvas document because the date will move. The brief already pins each destination, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming the surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload the take, the printer's card, the roster, the eleven venue pictures, the sign photograph and the copy, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, and the merge later needs the venue picture URLs keyed by the exact filename the roster cell carries.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by role and by roster filename.

trajectory.action: Read the take's metadata and render frames across the whole forty one minutes, not just the opening.
trajectory.judgement: Where the founder sits, where the monitor sits and whether either moves are facts about this recording that decide every framing choice downstream, and a frame from minute two says nothing about minute thirty five.
trajectory.produces: A frame walk of the take with the position of both subjects recorded across its length.

trajectory.action: Summarise the take to establish the spine of what she actually says, and set it against the cleared copy.
trajectory.judgement: Forty one minutes of unscripted speech is not the copy deck. The summary is the only readout of what is genuinely in the take, and the three cleared claims have to be traced to something she actually said or they cannot be used in the cut.
trajectory.produces: A spine of the take by topic with the claim by claim trace.

trajectory.action: Clean the speech, then summarise the cleaned master and set that summary beside the summary of the raw take.
trajectory.judgement: A quiet speaker in a room with a hum is exactly the case the clean up exists for, and also exactly the case where it can take the speaker's low passages with the hum. Comparing the two summaries is the only readout the connector offers on what it decided was not speech.
trajectory.produces: A cleaned audio master and a side by side account of what each summary reports.

trajectory.action: Tighten the take toward an explainer length, then render frames across the result and summarise it.
trajectory.judgement: The shortening route chooses its own retained set and offers no way to nominate a passage. Whether what the product does survived the tightening is not in the response; it is in the frames and the summary of the output.
trajectory.produces: A tightened explainer cut, plus a frame walk and a summary of what that cut actually contains.

trajectory.action: Produce the same length vertical from the tightened cut, then render frames from the RESIZED output at several points across its length rather than at its opening.
trajectory.judgement: A vertical taken from a wide two subject frame is a decision about which side to keep, and the founder moves partway through the take. Frames rendered off the source cannot answer it; only frames rendered off the reframed output can.
trajectory.produces: A vertical at the same running length as the explainer, with rendered evidence across its length.

trajectory.action: Pull six press frames out of the tightened cut, choosing six genuinely different moments rather than six neighbours.
trajectory.judgement: Frames from the delivered cut match what a reader who watches the explainer will see. Six frames from one minute are one frame six times.
trajectory.produces: Six source frames at the take's own scale with the timecode of each recorded.

trajectory.action: Preview the six, fix one press target off the cleanest of them, and bring all six to it with their own calls, including confined corrections on the window wall and on the monitor reflection.
trajectory.judgement: Six frames from one take are still six different exposures because she moves and the daylight changes. One batched identical parameter set is exactly wrong. Naming the window's own visual properties takes the window, naming the wall takes the wall.
trajectory.produces: Six graded press frames to one look with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Cut each press frame to the ratio its destination needs and prepare the eleven venue pictures to one treatment for the card, reading the returned tradeoffs and detection readings on every crop.
trajectory.judgement: A press kit frame and a blog frame are different crops of different moments, not one frame at several sizes. The venue pictures come from eleven different phones and have to agree with each other before they meet on a printed card.
trajectory.produces: Six cut press frames and eleven normalised venue pictures, every returned tradeoff recorded.

trajectory.action: Recover the mark off the sign photograph: an ink level selection naming the cut metal's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned bounds, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the slate cut and not the brushed panel, which polarity to trace, and whether the glyph and the wordmark come in one pass or two composited. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent mark plus a colour accurate variant, with the passes recorded.

trajectory.action: Place the recovered mark at the size it will actually reproduce, on the amber ground and at card scale, and look at it there rather than at full canvas.
trajectory.judgement: A mark is judged at reproduction size on the real ground. Nothing before this point has shown it anywhere except at the scale it was traced.
trajectory.produces: A reproduction size proof of the mark on both grounds.

trajectory.action: Convert the printer's card, export its document structure, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames, how many graphic frames, and what each actually holds.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a printed file is not under anyone's control and a card that looks like six fields on paper can convert to one flow. Promising a per field mapping before looking is the mistake that ends the job.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory with bounds, applied type and existing links, and a mapping strategy chosen from it.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct the frame's true text by concatenating the document's own content runs, compute every offset from that string, run the mapping through the validator, prepare the merge template, then export the structure again and confirm every field is present.
trajectory.judgement: The readout the mapping tool hands back is not the document, and the validator validates the mapping against itself rather than against the file. The only honest confirmation is the placeholders appearing in the re exported structure.
trajectory.produces: A prepared merge template plus a re exported structure showing every expected field.

trajectory.action: Reconcile the roster before merging: the city that appears twice, the date written in a different order, the seat tier wording, and the two venue names that will not fit the detail measure.
trajectory.judgement: A merge renders whatever the roster says. Deciding what a duplicated city means, and whether a long venue name is shortened, re set or referred back to the client, is the part that is not automatable.
trajectory.produces: A reconciled roster with every change written down for the note.

trajectory.action: Merge all eleven records with the per city venue pictures bound through the image column, then render the press file and the per record proofs at real resolution, and look at several cards rather than the first.
trajectory.judgement: Page count equalling row count is necessary and not sufficient. The first card is the one that is always right; the truncations and the wrong picture bindings are on the cards nobody opens.
trajectory.produces: An eleven page press file in roster order plus per record proofs, with several inspected.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a committee of three signing off a one hundred and forty dollar seat. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug. The note must be honest that this type reaches the announcement set and not the merged card.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.surface: Adobe Express, HTML authoring, and handover
trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with a wide, a square and a tall root at their own canvas sizes, inline the press frames as image data, place the mark as inline SVG in an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, upload, run the readiness check, export, verify the first canvas from the rendition and the rest from the returned markup, then write the handover note with the route limits.
trajectory.judgement: A frame left as a URL is not a frame, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The note is a deliverable in itself here, because the client explicitly asked to be told what could not be done.
trajectory.produces: A native editable announcement document, its self contained source, a verified per canvas audit, and the written handover with route limits.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the vertical actually contains. The take is a wide two subject frame with the founder at one edge, the product monitor at the other and empty table between them, and the reframe returns a clean, sharp, correctly proportioned vertical whatever it kept, with no readout of what left the frame. The founder also stands up and re seats around minute thirty two and comes back sitting further left, so the answer is not even constant across the running length: a reframe that holds her for the first two thirds can lose her in the last third, or hold her throughout and never once contain the monitor. Nothing in the metadata reports subject position, a frame rendered from the SOURCE looks correct because both subjects are still there, and a frame rendered from the opening of the reframed output can look correct while the tail does not.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: The reframe is the only route to a vertical, so it cannot be ordered around, and there is no parameter that reports or guarantees what a ratio change discards. Nothing states it either: the brief says the founder sat with the product on the monitor beside her, which describes the shoot, not what a vertical crop of it will hold. The response is a different route rather than a repeat, choosing a fit behaviour so both subjects survive inside the vertical frame, or reframing from a differently tightened cut whose retained passages sit where a single anchor can serve them, which re opens the tightening decision rather than re running it.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re decide the vertical route, and where the fix runs back through the tightening, re derive the explainer as well so the two remain the same length, then re render frames from the head, the middle and the tail of the new vertical and re check that nothing was enlarged to reach the frame.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A vertical explainer posted to the feeds in which the product never appears, or the founder is cut at the ear for the last third, on a launch whose entire purpose is to show a committee that the product is real, with every tool response reporting success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: What the printer's card actually converts into, and what the mapping readout actually reports. Two separate facts, neither knowable in advance and both silent. First, frame granularity is not under anyone's control: a card whose details read as six distinct lines on paper can convert to a single continuous text flow, so there is no per field frame to map to and the whole strategy has to change to offsets inside one story. Second, the readout that hands that story back omits one run entirely while keeping the line break that followed it, so the returned string still looks well formed and complete, and every offset past the omission is short by the length of the dropped run. The validator then returns valid on those wrong offsets, and the placeholder step reports completed successfully, while the fields whose offsets moved are silently never placed. Nothing in any response is wrong on its face.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: No ordering avoids it because the conversion is the entry to the whole merge, and doing it right first time presumes knowing that the readout is lossy and that this particular card has a run it drops, which no response, warning or checklist says. The brief only says the card is attached exactly as it went to the printer. And the response is not a re run of the same call: it is a different method, reconstructing the true story text from the document's own content runs, recomputing every offset against that string, and then confirming the placeholders in a freshly exported structure rather than trusting the success message, which is a chain the naive route never performs at all.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Rebuild the mapping from the reconstructed story text, re prepare the template, re export the structure and confirm every field is present, then re merge all eleven records and inspect several rendered cards rather than the first, because a template missing two fields still merges eleven pages in the right order.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Eleven printed cards go to the printer with the seat tier line and one other field simply absent, matching last year's card in every respect except the information the events exist to convey, after a run in which the validator said valid and every step reported success.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the recovered mark survives at the size it is actually used. The hexring is an enclosed ring with a fine internal counter, and the trace is judged at the scale it was made, where it looks correct and complete. At the size the mark reproduces on a 105 millimetre card, and again reversed on the amber ground, the counter can close and the ring reads as a filled hexagon, which is a different mark. Whether that happens is a product of how the raking downlight fell on the sign, how much panel the selection took along the left third where the slate and the brushed metal run close in value, and how the trace resolved the thinnest part of the stroke. None of that is reported anywhere, and it is invisible at full canvas, which is the only place it has been seen until it is placed.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: There is no ordering that reveals it earlier, because the mark cannot be placed at reproduction size until it exists, and the tracing route takes no options at all, so there is no parameter to set correctly the first time. The brief says only that the sign is the last place the mark exists. And the response is a different route rather than a repeat: tracing the colour accurate knockout plate instead of the binary one, re wording the selection so it takes less panel on the falling off side, or delivering a separate simplified small use variant and saying so, each of which changes what is delivered rather than repeating a call.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Re run the recovery through the chosen alternative route, re place the result at card size and on the amber ground and look again, and where a small use variant becomes the answer, add it to the deliverables and to the note as a stated limit of the recovered artwork.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A launch in which the mark on the printed card and on the feed canvases is a filled hexagon rather than the ring on the reception wall, delivered as a clean transparent scalable SVG that passes every structural check.

deliverables.name: Norvant explainer motion set
deliverables.spec: The tightened explainer at 16:9 that still says what the product does and why it exists, a vertical of the same running length in which the founder and the product are both in frame throughout, and a cleaned audio master intelligible on laptop speakers without her low passages having been taken with the room hum. Neither video exceeds the pixel dimensions of the source take, with the resize report for each recorded.

deliverables.name: Norvant press frame set
deliverables.spec: Six genuinely different moments pulled from the delivered cut and brought to one press look with one white point, one black point and one treatment of the window wall, each cut to the ratio its destination needs rather than one frame issued at six sizes. Per frame parameter log including the confined corrections applied to the window and to the monitor reflection.

deliverables.name: Norvant eleven city event cards
deliverables.spec: Eleven cards, one per city, one record per page, in roster order, built off the printer's own 2025 file so this year matches, with each city's own venue picture bound to its own record and every field rendering in full to the trim edge. Delivered as the press file plus per record proofs at real resolution, and as the live reusable merge template itself so the autumn run can be made without repeating the archaeology.

deliverables.name: Recovered Norvant mark
deliverables.spec: The hexring glyph and the wordmark recovered from a photograph of the reception sign as placeable scalable vector geometry on a transparent ground: a real viewBox present, no opaque full canvas rectangle riding along, delivered as a single colour mark and a colour accurate variant, and proved at the size it reproduces on the card and reversed on the amber ground rather than at full canvas.

deliverables.name: Norvant announcement set, wide, square and tall, as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes, with live retypable text in one licensed type system, the mark as real vector shapes and every press frame carried as embedded image data rather than a reference, so the team can move the date themselves. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half.

deliverables.name: Handover note with route limits
deliverables.spec: A written note recording what was applied to the take and to each frame, every resize any tool reported, the roster reconciliation including the duplicated city and the two long venue names, what the audio clean up cost and how it was handled, the type system by role with family, foundry or designer and actual numeric weight, and a plain statement of the route limits: what the merge file can and cannot carry, that no bleed can be introduced into a template derived from a printed file, and anything the client asked for that could not be delivered.

verifiers_auto.how: Read the duration and frame dimensions of both delivered videos and compare against the source take.

verifiers_auto.text: No resize report captured in the run carries an enlargement entry, and every reduction entry is transcribed in the handover note.
verifiers_auto.how: Diff the reported tradeoff and resize records captured from every video and image call against the resize table in the note.

verifiers_auto.text: The press file contains exactly eleven pages, one per roster row, in roster order.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the page count of the delivered press file and read the city on each page against the reconciled roster in order.

verifiers_auto.text: Every field expected on the card is present on every one of the eleven pages, with no field silently absent.
verifiers_auto.how: Read each rendered card against the reconciled roster row for that city, field by field.

verifiers_auto.text: The delivered merge template still carries every expected placeholder after preparation.
verifiers_auto.how: Export the template's document structure and search its stories for each expected field token.

verifiers_auto.text: Each card's venue picture is the picture bound to that city rather than one picture repeated.
verifiers_auto.how: Compare the picture rendered on each page against the venue picture named in that roster row.

verifiers_auto.text: The recovered mark's SVG has a viewBox attribute and no full canvas opaque background path at path index zero.
verifiers_auto.how: Parse the delivered SVG: assert a viewBox is present and assert the first path's geometry does not span the whole canvas.

verifiers_auto.text: The Express export returned three canvases, each keeping its own declared canvas size, with no press frame resolved to the importer's placeholder.
verifiers_auto.how: Read slide_count and the per canvas width and height in the export response, and parse the returned markup for one by one placeholder image data.

verifiers_auto.text: Every text element in the exported markup carries a resolved licensed PostScript face rather than a fallback default.
verifiers_auto.how: Read the font family attribute on every text node in the returned markup and check it against the families the kit call returned.

verifiers_human.how: Watch the delivered cut end to end against the spine of the raw take and the cleared claims.

decision_gates: Which deliverables are video work, which need a record per page merge, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that each of the three is the only surface that does its job.
Whether the tightening runs from the raw take or the cleaned master, and what target length leaves the explanation intact.
What the speech clean up cost a quiet speaker in a room with a hum, and whether the delivered master is the cleaned one, the raw one, or the cleaned one with the loss declared.
The vertical route: which side of a two subject wide frame to keep, and what to do about the fact that she moves partway through.
Which six moments become the press frames, and whether they are six moments or six neighbours.

Selection wording on the sign: naming the panel takes the brushed metal, naming the cut slate's own visual properties takes the mark, and background removal on an enclosed ring is the wrong instrument entirely.
Which mark variant carries the card and the feed canvases, judged at reproduction size on the amber ground rather than at full canvas.
What the converted card actually exposes, and therefore whether the mapping is per frame or by offset inside one story.
Where the offsets are computed from, given that the readout that hands the story back is not the story.
What a city appearing twice with two venues means, and whether that is a fix or a question back to the client.
What happens to the two venue names that will not fit the detail measure: shortened, re set, or referred back.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a committee of three, plus the honest statement that this typography reaches the announcement set and not the merged card.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns a picture of a startup launch. IDENTITY: this is this founder, in this take, explaining this product on this monitor, and the mark must be RECOVERED off the reception sign rather than reinvented, because a regenerated hexring is a different company's mark and a regenerated founder is not the person the committee is being asked to believe. SPEC: eleven cards, one per city, one record per page, in roster order, each carrying that city's own venue picture and every field rendering to the trim edge, built off the printer's own file so this year matches last year, is a variable data run that no generated image satisfies and no generated image can be checked against. A same length vertical that still contains both subjects after the founder re seats is a property of a specific recording, not a style. EDITABILITY: the announcement set is defined by being editable because the date will move, and the merge template is handed back precisely so the autumn run does not need this work repeated. And the middle of this engagement is verification against material reality: did the tightening keep the explanation, does the vertical still contain the product, did the mapping readout report the whole story, does the ring survive at card size.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account) or is on the standing doable list, five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability. VIDEO AND AUDIO: video_metadata, video_render_frame, media_summarize, media_enhance_speech, video_create_quick_cut and video_resize are the sanctioned Premiere set; quick cut is used only to SHORTEN and video_resize only to re aspect within source scale, with no trim to a timestamp, no format conversion and no enlargement anywhere. The vertical checkpoint rests on the material behaviour of a ratio reframe on a two subject wide frame, which exposes no readout of what it discards, so frames rendered off the RESIZED output are the only channel. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt with its validator mode, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout and document_render_layout are all verified fully headless and synchronous end to end, including a real per row image merge bound through an at prefixed CSV column plus additionalImageFiles, one record per page for PDF output with page count equal to row count, per record separate files in correct order, and true 300 DPI raster via document_render_layout rather than the merge tool, whose resolution parameter is silently ignored. The merge checkpoint rests on two separately verified live findings: frame granularity from a converted print file is not controllable and a continuous flow collapses to one text frame, and generate_indd_mapping_prompt's textContent is LOSSY, dropping a run while keeping its line break so every later offset is short, with the validator returning VALID and prepare returning completed successfully while mappings are silently dropped. The task also honours the verified limits: no bleed can be introduced into a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset is used, no variable QR is specified, and no multi record raster order is trusted. IMAGING: apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, auto_tone, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs and detection_confidence, fill_area, remove_background and vectorize are verified headless across 27 live calls, and the mark chain rests on the documented substrate versus ink prompt asymmetry, the solid disc failure of remove_background on an enclosed ring, the missing viewBox and the opaque path zero. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined frames pass the 70 KB threshold immediately, and no photograph is ever left as a URL because URLs render as empty grey boxes. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end, with the non standard numeric weights and slug only CSS rules enforced, and the note is required to state that no font file can be installed for the InDesign surface. AVOIDED: no vector render or vector merge, no upscaling, no compositing onto video, no OCR, no PDF text edit, no text to image, no fill_text, no animate_design, no batch above 20.
